stories.headline: Carney launches major trade mission to India, Australia and Japan seeking to diversify from US
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney embarked on a 9-day trade mission (Feb 26-Mar 7) to India, Australia and Japan, meeting with Modi, Albanese and other leaders to secure new trade deals and reduce Canada's dependence on the United States. The trip resulted in $5.5 billion in commercial agreements including a $2.6 billion uranium deal with Saskatchewan.

stories.headline: Poilievre delivers major speech on Canada-US relations, critiques Carney's China pivot
stories.summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre gave a significant policy speech at the Economic Club of Canada on Feb 26, laying out his vision for managing trade relations with the US under Trump. He argued China cannot substitute for the US and criticized Carney's approach while proposing an all-party working group on USMCA review.

stories.headline: Conservative MP Matt Jeneroux crosses floor to Liberals, joins Carney's India trade delegation
stories.summary: Edmonton-Riverbend MP Matt Jeneroux became the third Conservative MP to defect to the Liberals in recent months, with Carney immediately appointing him as special advisor on economic and security partnerships and including him in the India trade mission. The move brings the Liberals closer to a potential majority.

stories.headline: Canada supports US-Israeli strikes on Iran nuclear facilities, Carney announces from India
stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney voiced Canada's support for US and Israeli military strikes against Iran's nuclear program while on his trade mission in Mumbai. The announcement drew criticism from the NDP and raised questions about consultation with Parliament. Iran has threatened retaliation for the attacks.

stories.headline: Canada's Big Six banks report strong Q1 2026 earnings, exceed expectations
stories.summary: All of Canada's major banks exceeded profit forecasts for the first quarter of 2026, with RBC reporting $5.79 billion in profit and National Bank posting strong loan growth. The results were boosted by wealth management and capital markets strength, showing economic resilience despite trade uncertainty.

stories.headline: Liberal polling surge continues as Carney maintains strong lead over Poilievre
stories.summary: Multiple polls show the Liberals maintaining a significant lead over the Conservatives, with some surveys putting the gap at 12 points. Carney's personal approval ratings remain well ahead of Poilievre's, and turnout projections favor the Liberals. The trend has sparked speculation about a potential snap election.

stories.headline: Canada's economy contracts in Q4 2025, raising questions about BoC growth forecasts
stories.summary: Statistics Canada reported the economy shrank 0.6% in the fourth quarter of 2025, worse than expected and below Bank of Canada projections. The contraction was driven by inventory drawdowns despite growth in exports and household spending. Economists are questioning whether BoC growth targets for 2026 are achievable.

stories.summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre will travel to London and Berlin next week for his first official overseas trip as opposition leader, meeting with parliamentary colleagues and business leaders. The trip comes as Carney is traveling to Asia and represents Poilievre's effort to build international Conservative relationships.

stories.summary: The federal NDP leadership contest continues with low energy and minimal media attention as the party tries to rebuild after losing official party status in 2025. Five candidates are vying to replace Jagmeet Singh, with debates focusing on whether to prioritize electoral success or movement building.

stories.headline: Bloc Québécois and Liberals set for rematch in Terrebonne byelection
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ordered a new election in Terrebonne after the original result was decided by a single vote. Bloc candidate Nathalie Sinclair-Desgagné and Liberal candidate Tatiana Auguste will face each other again in a race that could determine whether the Carney government can achieve a majority.

stories.headline: Canadian Armed Forces applications surge 13% amid global uncertainty
stories.summary: Defence Minister David McGuinty announced that CAF applications have increased 13% over the past eight months, which he attributes to Canadians' desire to ensure national security. The military is working to rebuild to 71,500 regular force members by 2032 under the 'Our North, Strong and Free' plan.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney unveiled Canada's new industrial defence policy aimed at growing the domestic defence industry and creating up to 125,000 jobs. The strategy emphasizes building military equipment at home and strengthening defence supply chains amid growing global security challenges.
